additions.source_text_quote: וְזֶה נִקְרָא: מֹאזְנֵי צֶדֶק (ויקרא י״ט:ל״ו), כִּי צֶדֶק מַלְכוּתָא קַדִּישָׁא, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת כָּבוֹד, מֶלֶךְ הַכָּבוֹד כַּנַּ"ל
additions.note: In line 3, the Rebbe names the scales of judgment 'מֹאזְנֵי צֶדֶק' and then provides a theological gloss: צֶדֶק is the Zoharic name for מַלְכוּתָא קַדִּישָׁא (Holy Kingship — the sefirah of Malkhut). He then states: 'שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת כָּבוֹד' — IT is a bechina of כָּבוֹד. The phrase 'שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת' is canonical Breslov bechina-identification language. The referent of 'שֶׁהוּא' is the entire preceding clause: צֶדֶק/מַלְכוּתָא קַדִּישָׁא. The Rebbe then confirms the equation with 'מֶלֶךְ הַכָּבוֹד כַּנַּ"ל' — the King of Honor, as stated above (referring back to Psalm 24:7 cited in line 1). This is a double bechina chain: (A) צֶדֶק = מַלְכוּתָא קַדִּישָׁא (standard Zoharic equation, implicitly bechina); (B) מַלְכוּתָא קַדִּישָׁא = כָּבוֹד (explicit bechina via 'שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת'). Since מַלְכוּת is already equated with כָּבוֹד in the dataset (edge 1826), this addition specifically proposes the edge צֶדֶק ↔ כָּבוֹד (or equivalently צֶדֶק ↔ מַלְכוּת, with מַלְכוּת serving as the bridge). The most direct missing edge that closes the triangle is צֶדֶק ↔ כָּבוֹד, though צֶדֶק ↔ מַלְכוּת would also capture the Zoharic equation. Both are proposed; precedence goes to the one that adds a new connection not already derivable by transitivity from the existing dataset.

candidates_examined_and_excluded.reason_excluded: The phrase 'וְזֶה נִקְרָא: מֹאזְנֵי צֶדֶק' ('and this is called scales of justice') names the process of weighing — it identifies the מאזנים (scales) as the instrument through which כבוד/מלכות/צדק judges. This is an eitza-context identification (the scales are the mechanism of the judgment process), not a bechina equation between מאזני צדק and one of the core bechina-cluster nodes. The scales are named after צדק (which IS the cluster) — but the scales themselves are not an aspect of the same nature as כבוד/מלכות/צדק; they are the judicial instrument of that nature. Excluded from package nodes.

candidates_examined_and_excluded.concept: מְכֻבָּדִי (those who honor Me / My honored ones)
candidates_examined_and_excluded.source_text: אַל תִּקְרֵי בִּכְבוֹדִי, אֶלָּא בִּמְכֻבָּדִי (זבחים קטו:)
candidates_examined_and_excluded.reason_excluded: The Talmudic drasha ('do not read bichvodi/with My glory — but bimchubadai/with those who honor Me') is a hermeneutic pivot that reinterprets the verse to show that mishandling כבוד can cause death (Nadav and Avihu). The word מכובדי is a textual emendation used to make a homiletic point — it is not being equated with כבוד or מלכות as a conceptual parallel. It is an explanation of the danger of כבוד in practice. Excluded.

This is a biblical divine title (Psalm 24:7) cited as the proof-text for the כבוד = מלכות equation. 'מֶלֶךְ הַכָּבוֹד' is the scriptural formulation that bridges the two concepts — it is the evidence for the bechina, not itself a separate conceptual node requiring its own package slot. The Rebbe treats it as the textual grounding for the identification, not as a third independent concept. It could be argued that 'מלך הכבוד' is an alias or appellation of the כבוד/מלכות cluster, but since the Rebbe introduces it as a citation supporting the already-named bechina, and uses 'כַּנַּ"ל' (as stated) in line 3 to refer back to it, it functions as a proof-text anchor, not a distinct bechina node. Excluded as redundant given the existing cluster.
